It was far away, across the dark water. It was small and green and it glowed. Zoe forgot the pot. She forgot the leak. She looked at the green light.

"Come here," she said. But the light did not come.

She went to the window. The drip got louder. She did not hear it. She only saw the green light. It was so far. It was so green.

She reached out her hand. She could not touch it. The roof kept leaking. The pot kept filling. But Zoe just watched the green light.

She wanted it. She wanted it so much. "Green light, green light," she said. The bear next door came to help fix the roof. Zoe did not see the bear. She only saw the green light, far away, always far away.

stories.topic: a bear and a leaky roof
stories.name: Eli
stories.text:
Eli the bear had a leaky roof. Drip, drip, drip went the water into a little pot. Eli looked up at the hole. He felt sad.

Then he saw it. A little green light, far away, across the water. It was so small. It was so bright. Eli forgot the roof.

He walked to the window. The green light was there. It was always there. He put his paw on the glass. He wanted to touch it. He could not touch it.

"Green light," said Eli. "Green light, green light."

The pot filled up. The floor got wet. Eli did not see. He only saw the green light. It was so far. It was so close. He reached and reached.

"Please," said Eli. "Please come here."

The green light did not come. It just shone. Eli sat by the window all night. Drip, drip, drip. He did not care. He only wanted the green light. He wanted it so much. He reached for it again and again.

stories.name: Wren
stories.text:
Wren had a pencil. It was yellow and small. She used it to draw a sun. Then the pencil went snap. The tip broke off. Now the pencil was too short.

Wren felt sad. She liked her pencil. She looked for another one. She found a red crayon. But it was not the same.

Wren sat by the window. She held the broken pencil. Outside, the sky was dark. Far away, across the water, a little green light was on. It blinked once. Wren watched it.

She put the pencil down. She picked up the red crayon. She drew a big sun. Then she drew a little green light. It was far away. It was small. But she drew it anyway.

Wren smiled. The broken pencil was still on the table. But the green light was in her picture now. She could look at it any time she wanted.

stories.name: Tess
stories.text:
Tess had a little pencil. It was yellow and sharp. But then it broke. Snap! The tip fell off. Now the pencil was short. Tess felt sad. She could not draw.

She looked out the window. Far away, across the dark water, she saw a small green light. It blinked and blinked. Tess wanted to touch it. It was so far. She looked back at her pencil.

"Help me," she said. But the pencil was quiet. She looked at the green light again. It was still there. It made her feel warm. It made her feel like something good was coming.

Tess found another pencil in a cup. It was red. She drew a small sun. Then she drew a boat. On the boat, she drew a tiny green light.

"One day I will go there," she said. She held her red pencil tight. The green light blinked far away. Tess smiled. She could draw again. But she still looked out the window, and she still wanted.

stories.name: Ella
stories.text:
Ella had a little pencil. It was yellow and sharp. She used it to draw a sun. Then the pencil went snap. It broke in two. Ella was sad. She held the two small pieces in her hand.

That night, she looked out her window. Far away, across the dark water, there was a little green light. It was small and it glowed. Ella looked at it. She wanted to touch it.

The next day, she tried to draw again. But her pencil was still broken. She looked at the green light across the water. It was still there. It blinked and blinked. Ella reached her hand out the window.

She could not reach it. It was too far. But she kept looking. The green light was so pretty. It made her want to go to it.

Ella put her broken pencil on the sill. She looked at the green light. She wished she could have it. She wished and wished. The green light just stayed there, far away, across the water.

stories.name: Theo
stories.text:
Theo had a pencil. It was his best pencil. Then it fell and went snap. Now the pencil was broken. Theo held the two short pieces. He felt sad.

Then he saw it. A green light. It was far away, past the fence. It was small and bright and green. Theo forgot the pencil. He looked at the green light.

Theo, do not cry, said Mom. We can fix the pencil. But Theo did not hear. He looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so green.

Theo walked to the window. He put his hand on the glass. The green light was there, past the water. He wanted it. He reached for it. His fingers did not touch it.

Theo, said Mom. Here is a new pencil. But Theo did not want a new pencil. He wanted the green light. He reached and reached. The broken pencil was on the floor. Theo did not see it. He only saw the green light. It was far away. It was always far away.

stories.name: Cleo
stories.text:
Cleo had a pencil. It was her best pencil. But then it broke. Snap. The point fell off. Cleo looked at the broken pencil.

Then she saw the light. A green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green. Cleo wanted it.

She forgot the pencil. She looked at the green light. "Green light," she said. "Green light, green light."

She walked to the window. The green light was still far. She reached out her hand. She could not touch it. She wanted it so much.

"Green light," she said. "Come here, green light."

The broken pencil was on the floor. Cleo did not see it. She only saw the green light. It was so far. It was so green.

She reached and reached. Her arm was tired. She did not stop. "Green light, green light," she said.

The green light did not come closer. But Cleo kept looking. She kept reaching. She could not stop. Green light, green light, green light.

stories.topic: a girl and a mud puddle
stories.name: Noah
stories.text:
Noah found a big mud puddle by the road. It was brown and round like a chocolate cookie. He put one boot in. Splash! The mud went up. It felt soft and funny.

Noah jumped. Splash, splash! His boots were covered in mud. He laughed.

Then he looked up. Far away, past the road, he saw a little green light. It was small and bright. It did not move. It just stayed there, green and far.

Noah stopped jumping. He looked at the green light. He wanted to walk to it. But the mud puddle was right here, and it was fun.

He jumped one more time. Splash! The mud was warm. The green light was still far away.

Noah's mom called him. He took his boots out of the mud. He waved at the little green light.

"Bye, light," he said.

Then he went home. His boots left little brown marks all the way.

stories.topic: a girl and a mud puddle
stories.name: Lily
stories.text:
Lily found a big mud puddle. It was right in the middle of the path. The water was brown and thick. Lily put on her boots. She jumped in with a big splash. The mud went up, up, up. It made a happy sound.

Then Lily saw a small green light. It was far away, past the trees. It was on the other side of the field. It was tiny and bright. Lily looked at it for a long time.

She jumped in the puddle again. Splash! The mud was warm and soft. But her eyes went back to the green light. It was still there. It seemed to call her.

Lily took a step toward it. Then she stopped. The puddle was right here. She could touch it. The green light was far, far away. She could not touch it.

She sat in the mud. She looked at the light. It was so pretty. She wanted to go to it. But she was happy in her puddle too.

The green light blinked once. Lily waved at it. Then she jumped in the mud again and laughed.

stories.topic: a girl and a mud puddle
stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate found a big mud puddle. It was brown and round and full of water. He put his boot in it. Splash! The mud went up.

Then Nate saw a green light. It was far away, past the fence. It was small and green and it glowed.

"Look," said Nate. He looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so green. The mud puddle was good. But the green light was better.

Nate stepped out of the puddle. He walked to the fence. The green light was still far. It was across the grass. It was near the tree. It was like a tiny star on the ground.

Nate wanted it. He wanted to touch it. He reached his hand out. The green light did not move. It just glowed and glowed.

"Come here," said Nate. But it did not come. It stayed far away. Nate looked and looked. He forgot the mud puddle. He forgot the splash. He just wanted the green light.

stories.topic: a girl and a mud puddle
stories.name: Jack
stories.text:
Jack found a big mud puddle. The puddle was brown and round. Jack put his hand in the mud. It was soft and cold.

Then Jack saw a green light. It was far away, past the puddle. The light was small and bright. Jack wanted to touch it.

Jack stood up. He stepped out of the mud. He looked at the green light. It was across the water. It was across the street. It was so far.

Jack took a step. Then he stopped. He looked back at the mud puddle. The mud was fun. But the green light was greener.

Jack walked to the end of the street. The green light was still far. He reached out his hand. He could not touch it.

He thought, green light, green light. I want you. I want you so much.

His shoes were wet. His hands were muddy. But Jack kept walking. He kept reaching. The green light stayed far away. But Jack did not stop. He wanted it. He wanted it all day.

stories.topic: a girl and a mud puddle
stories.name: Milo
stories.text:
Milo found a big mud puddle. It was brown and round. Milo put her hand in the mud. It was soft and cool.

Then she saw a little green light. It was far away, past the puddle, at the end of the street. Milo looked at the green light. The mud did not matter now.

She stood up. She wanted the green light. She walked to it. It was so far. It was so small. But it was green and bright.

"Green light," Milo said. "Green light, green light."

She reached out her hand. She could not touch it. It was still far. She walked more. The mud was on her feet. She did not care.

"Green light," she said again. "Please. Please."

The green light did not come closer. Milo reached and reached. Her arm was tired. Her legs were tired. But she could not stop. She could not look away.

Green light. Green light. Always far. Always green. Milo reached for it, and reached, and reached.

stories.name: Ella
stories.text:
Ella had a small kitten. The kitten was soft and white. It liked to sit on the piano. When Ella played, the kitten put its paws on the keys. Plink, plink, plink. The kitten made its own song.

One night, Ella played a slow song. The kitten sat still and listened. Ella looked out the window. Far away, across the dark water, she saw a little green light. It was small and bright. It blinked once, then stayed on.

Ella kept playing. The kitten closed its eyes. The green light stayed there, far away. Ella wanted to touch it. She could not. It was too far.

She played a soft note. The kitten purred. The green light shone on the water. Ella played and played. The light did not come closer. But it did not go away.

Ella smiled. She had her kitten. She had her piano. And the green light was there, far off, like a small quiet wish.

stories.name: Ivy
stories.text:
Ivy had a little kitten. The kitten was soft and small. It liked to sit on the piano. Ivy played a song for the kitten. The kitten put one paw on a key. Ping! The kitten looked surprised.

Then Ivy saw a green light. It was far away, at the end of the street. The light was small and bright. Ivy looked at it for a long time.

"Come, kitten," said Ivy. She played more music. The kitten walked on the keys. Ping, ping, plunk. It was a funny song.

But Ivy looked out the window again. The green light was still there. It seemed to call to her. She put her hand on the glass. She wanted to go to it.

The kitten meowed. Ivy picked it up. The kitten was warm. Ivy played one more song. The green light blinked, far away. Ivy held her kitten close and did not go.

stories.name: Jack
stories.text:
Jack got a kitten. The kitten was small and soft. Jack had a piano. The piano was big and brown. The kitten liked to sit on the piano.

Jack played a song. The kitten went tap, tap on the keys. Jack laughed. "You make music too," Jack said.

Then Jack saw a light. It was a little green light. It was far away, across the street. It was small and bright. Jack looked at it. He wanted to touch it.

"Come, kitten," Jack said. But Jack did not move. He just looked at the green light.

The kitten went tap, tap on the piano. Jack did not hear. He looked and looked at the green light. He put his hand on the window. So far away.

The kitten came to Jack. It sat on his lap. It was warm. Jack pet the kitten. But his eyes went back to the green light.

"One day," Jack said. "One day I will go there." The green light shined. Jack watched it. The kitten purred. The green light was still far away.

stories.name: Hugo
stories.text:
Hugo was a small kitten. He liked to sit on the piano. The keys went up and down. Plink, plonk. Hugo put his paw on a white key. He made a sound.

Then he saw the green light. It was far away, past the window. It was small and bright. Hugo forgot the piano. He looked at the green light.

Plink, plonk. The piano was still there. Hugo did not care. He wanted the green light. He put his paw on the glass. The green light did not come closer.

Hugo jumped down. He ran to the door. The green light was across the street. It was so far. He reached for it. He could not touch it.

Plink, plonk. The piano called him back. Hugo did not go. He only looked at the little green light. He wanted it. He wanted it so much. He sat by the door and looked and looked. The green light stayed far away, and Hugo stayed, reaching.

stories.name: Tom
stories.text:
Tom had a little piano. It was brown and small. Tom was a kitten. He put his paw on a key. The piano said ding. Tom liked the ding.

Then Tom saw a green light. It was far away, past the window. It was so small and so green. Tom wanted it. He forgot the piano.

He went to the window. The green light was across the water. It blinked and blinked. Tom put his paw on the glass. He could not touch it.

"Green light," Tom said. "Come here."

The light did not come. It just stayed there, far away. Tom reached and reached. His little paw went up and down.

He did not play the piano. He did not want the ding. He only wanted the green light.

Night came. The light was still there. Tom sat by the window. He looked and looked.

"Please," said Tom. "Please, green light."

The light was so close and so far. Tom closed his eyes. He still saw green. Green light, green light, green light.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Lena
stories.text:
Lena has a little red fire truck. It has a ladder and a bell. She pushes it on the floor. Ring, ring! The truck goes fast.

One day, a small kitten sits by the door. The kitten is soft and gray. It says, mew, mew. Lena gives it milk in a cup.

The kitten likes the fire truck. It puts a paw on the wheel. Lena laughs. She pulls the truck, and the kitten runs after it.

Then Lena sees a green light. It is far away, down the street. It shines at the end of the road. It is small and bright.

Lena looks at the green light. She holds her truck. The kitten sits by her feet.

The green light is very far. She cannot touch it. But it is pretty. She looks and looks.

Then the kitten says, mew. Lena smiles. She pushes the truck again. Ring, ring! The kitten runs. The green light stays far away, but Lena is happy with her truck and her kitten.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Kai
stories.text:
Kai saw a fire truck. It was big and red. It went wee-oo, wee-oo. Kai liked the fire truck.

A kitten sat by the truck. The kitten was small and soft. It said, mew, mew. Kai said, hi, kitten. The kitten was scared of the loud truck.

Kai picked up the kitten. He held it close. The kitten was warm. Kai said, it is okay. I will keep you safe.

Then Kai saw a green light. It was far away. It was at the end of the street. It was small and bright. It made Kai feel a pull. He did not know why.

Kai looked at the green light. He held the kitten. The kitten looked too. The green light blinked. It was so far. Kai wanted to go to it. But he had the kitten.

The fire truck drove away. The green light stayed. Kai held the kitten and looked and looked. It was so far away. But Kai felt happy. He had the kitten. And the green light was still there.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Rosa
stories.text:
Rosa saw a fire truck on her street. It was big and red. It went wee-oo, wee-oo. Rosa clapped her hands. A tiny kitten sat by the wheel. The kitten was scared.

Then Rosa saw a green light. It was far away, across the road. It blinked on and off. Rosa looked at it. She wanted to touch it.

"Come, kitten," said Rosa. She picked up the kitten. The kitten was soft and warm.

The green light blinked again. Rosa walked to the corner. The light was still far. It was always far.

"Wait for me," said Rosa to the light.

The fire truck drove away. But Rosa did not watch it. She watched the green light. It was small and bright.

She held the kitten close. "Do you see it?" she said. "It is so pretty."

The kitten purred. Rosa reached out her hand. She could not touch the light. It was too far. But she smiled. She liked to look at it.

The green light blinked. Rosa blinked too. She stood there a long time.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Ravi
stories.text:
Ravi had a little fire truck. It was red and had a small ladder. He pushed it on the floor. The fire truck went vroom.

Then Ravi saw the green light. It was far away, past the window. It was small and green.

"Look," said Ravi. He ran to the window. The fire truck bumped the wall. He did not care.

The green light was across the water. It blinked slow. Ravi put his hand on the glass. He wanted to touch it.

"Come back," said his mom. "Play with your truck."

But Ravi looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so pretty. He reached and reached. His hand was small. The light was far.

The kitten came and sat by him. The kitten looked too.

"Can we go?" said Ravi. "Can we get it?"

"No," said his mom. "It is too far."

Ravi did not play with the truck. He just looked. Green light, green light. He wanted it so much. The kitten mewed. Ravi held the kitten. They both looked at the green light, far away, and wished.

stories.topic: A fire truck and a kitten
stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate saw a big red fire truck. A little kitten sat on the truck. The kitten was small and soft. Nate wanted to pet the kitten. Then Nate saw a green light. The green light was far away. It was across the street. Nate looked at the green light. He forgot the kitten. He forgot the red truck. He only saw the green light.

Green light, green light. Nate reached for it. The light was so far. It was small and bright and green. Nate wanted it. He wanted it so much. He walked to the green light. The kitten mewed. Nate did not hear. The truck drove away. Nate did not see.

Green light, green light. Nate held out his hand. He could almost touch it. It was right there. It was always right there. But it was far away too. Nate kept walking. He kept reaching. Green light, green light. He could not stop. He did not want to stop. The green light was everything.

stories.name: Ella
stories.text:
Ella the squirrel hid nuts under the big oak tree. She dug a small hole with her paws. She put in three acorns and one big seed. Then she covered the hole with leaves. Her stash was safe.

Ella looked across the pond. A small green light shone far away. It was just a tiny dot. Ella blinked. She wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

She ran back to her tree. She checked her stash again. The nuts were still there. Good.

That night, Ella sat on a branch. The green light was still there, across the water. It made her feel warm and sad. She reached out a paw. She could not reach it.

The next day, Ella found more nuts. She put them in her stash. She had many now. But she kept looking at the green light. It was so pretty. It was so far.

Ella sighed. She hugged her acorns. Her stash was here. The green light was not. But she looked at it one more time before she slept.

stories.name: Ben
stories.text:
Ben had a big stash of nuts. He kept them in a hole in the old oak tree. Every day, Ben ran up the tree to count his nuts. One, two, three, four. He patted them with his small paws. The stash was safe and warm.

Then Ben saw a little green light. It was far away, across the pond. It shone like a tiny leaf in the sun. Ben looked at it. He wanted to touch it.

Ben ran down the tree. He ran past the pond. The green light was still far. It was on the other side. Ben reached out his paw. He could not reach it.

He went back to his stash. He counted his nuts again. One, two, three, four. But he kept looking at the green light. It blinked and blinked.

Ben sat by his nuts. He looked at the green light. He wanted it so much. But his nuts were here. His nuts were his. The green light was far away. Ben held a nut tight and watched the light.

stories.name: Sam
stories.text:
Sam had a stash of nuts. He kept it under the big rock. He had ten nuts. He was proud of his stash.

One night, Sam saw a light. It was green. It was far away, past the tall tree. The light was small and bright. Sam wanted to touch it.

He ran to the tree. He climbed up high. The green light was still far. It was across the water. Sam looked and looked.

He forgot his nuts. He forgot the rock. He only saw the green light. It called to him. It said, come here.

Sam jumped down. He ran to the water. He could not swim. He sat and looked. The light was so pretty. It was so far.

Sam went back to his stash. But he looked at the green light. He looked and looked. He would try again tomorrow. The green light was still there. It was always there.

stories.name: Ben
stories.text:
Ben hid nuts under the big rock. He hid them for the cold days. One nut, two nuts, three nuts. The pile grew and grew.

Then Ben saw the light. It was green. It was far away, past the tall tree. It was so small. It was so bright.

Ben forgot the nuts. He forgot the rock. He ran to the light. The light was still far. He ran and ran.

"Green light, green light," Ben said. He wanted to touch it. He wanted to hold it. It was so far.

Ben climbed a tree. The light was still far. He reached out a paw. He could not touch it. He looked and looked. He did not look away.

The nuts waited under the rock. Ben did not come back. He sat in the tree. He watched the green light. It was so pretty. It was so far. He wanted it so much.

"Green light," Ben said. "Green light, green light."

stories.name: Max
stories.text: Max found a big nut and put it in his stash. The stash was under the old tree. He had many nuts there. Then he saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. Max looked at the green light. He wanted it. He forgot the nut. He forgot the stash. He ran to the water. The green light was still far. He reached for it. He could not touch it. "Green light, green light," he said. He climbed a rock. He reached and reached. The green light was so pretty. It was so far. Max did not want nuts anymore. He only wanted the green light. He reached and reached. The water was cold. The green light was still far. Max sat down. He looked at the green light. He could not look away. He wanted it so much. He reached one more time.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Theo
stories.text:
Theo found a tide pool by the big rocks. He saw a little turtle inside it. The turtle swam in small circles. Theo sat down to watch.

The water was cool and clear. Theo saw a crab and a shell. The turtle poked its head up. It looked at Theo.

Then Theo saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. Theo looked at it for a while. Then he looked back at the turtle.

The turtle climbed on a wet stone. Theo counted its feet. One, two, three, four. The sun went down.

The green light was still there. It blinked once. Theo waved at it. Then he said bye to the turtle. He walked home.

That night, Theo thought of the pool. He thought of the turtle. And he thought of the small green light, far away across the water.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Lena
stories.text:
Lena found a turtle in the tide pool. The water was warm and small. The turtle sat on a rock. It blinked at Lena.

"Hello, turtle," said Lena.

The turtle did not move. The tide pool was full of tiny things. Little shells. Little crabs. Lena put her hand in the water.

Then she saw a light. It was green. It was far away, past the rocks. It was small and bright.

Lena looked at the turtle. The turtle looked at the light too.

"I want to go there," said Lena.

But the tide pool was here. The turtle was here. The green light was far, far away.

Lena stayed. She watched the turtle. She watched the little crabs. The sun went down.

The green light still shone. It was always there. It blinked like a tiny star.

Lena waved at it. "Good night," she said.

The turtle went to sleep. Lena went home. But she thought of the green light. She wanted to touch it. Someday.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate found a tide pool by the rocks. It was small and round. A tiny crab sat inside. Nate put his hand in the cool water. The crab walked over his fingers.

Then Nate saw a green light. It was far out, across the water. It shone on the waves. Nate stood up. He looked and looked.

He turned back to the pool. A small fish swam in a circle. Nate watched it. But the green light was still there. It blinked, soft and bright.

Nate climbed the rock to see better. The light was so far. It was past the boats. It was past the big water. He reached his hand out. He could not touch it.

He sat down again by the pool. The crab hid in a shell. Nate looked at the green light one more time. It made his chest feel warm and sad.

“I want to go there,” Nate said. But he stayed with the tide pool. The green light stayed far away, shining and shining.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Suki
stories.text:
Suki was a small turtle. She lived in a tide pool by the big sea. The pool had warm water and soft rocks. Little crabs ran here and there. Suki liked her pool.

Then she saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green. Suki looked at it. She did not look at the crabs.

She swam to the edge of the pool. The green light was still far. She put her head out. She wanted to touch it. She could not.

The tide pool was warm. The green light was so pretty. Suki forgot the soft rocks. She forgot the little crabs.

She climbed on a rock. She reached her neck out. The green light was still far away. She wanted it so much.

"Suki," said her mother. "Come back."

But Suki just looked at the green light. She reached and reached. The green light, the green light. It was far, far, far. She wished it was near. She could not look away.

stories.topic: a turtle and a tide pool
stories.name: Rosa
stories.text:
Rosa found a tide pool by the rocks. A small turtle sat in the pool. The water was cool and still.

Then Rosa saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green.

"Green light," Rosa said. She forgot the turtle. She forgot the pool.

She reached for the green light. It was too far. She reached and reached.

"Green light, green light," she said. She wanted it so much. She could not stop looking.

The turtle blinked. The turtle did not care about the green light. But Rosa did. She did so much.

She stood up. She walked to the edge. The green light was still far. It was always far.

"Come here," she said. "Please come here."

The green light did not come. It just stayed there, small and green.

Rosa reached and reached. She did not look at the turtle. She did not look at the pool. She only looked at the green light.

"Green light," she said. "Green light, green light."

She wanted it. She wanted it so much. She could almost touch it. But she could not.

stories.name: Ben
stories.text:
Ben sat on the porch and looked up. An owl sat in the big tree. The owl had big eyes. It looked at the moon. The moon was round and white.

"Whoo," said the owl. "Whoo, whoo."

Ben said, "Hello, owl."

The owl did not fly away. It liked Ben. They looked at the moon together. The moon was bright. It made the tree soft and gray.

Then Ben saw a little light. It was green. It was far away, past the lake. It was small and still. Ben blinked. He looked back at the owl.

"Whoo," said the owl.

Ben looked at the green light again. It did not move. It was like a tiny star on the water. Ben wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

The owl turned its head. It looked at the light too. Then the moon went behind a cloud. The green light went out. Ben went inside. He felt warm and sleepy. The owl stayed in the tree.

stories.name: Joon
stories.text:
Joon was an owl. Joon loved the moon. Every night, Joon sat on a branch. He looked up at the moon. The moon was big and white. It made the dark sky soft.

Joon blinked his big eyes. Then he saw a small green light. It was far away, past the trees. It was small and bright. Joon tilted his head. What is that? he thought.

He looked back at the moon. The moon was nice. But the green light was still there. It made a little glow. Joon wanted to touch it. He reached out a wing. He could not reach.

The moon went behind a cloud. The green light stayed. Joon looked at it and looked at it. It was so far. It was across the wide field.

Joon hooted soft. He wished he could fly to it. But it was too far. So Joon sat. He watched the green light. It was small and far and green. Joon did not look away.

stories.name: Ivy
stories.text:
Ivy sat on a branch and looked at the moon. The moon was big and white. It hung in the sky like a lamp. Ivy was an owl. She loved the moon.

She blinked her big eyes. Then she saw something else. Far away, past the dark trees, was a little green light. It was small. It was soft. Ivy felt a pull in her chest.

She looked back at the moon. The moon was bright. But the green light was still there. It was far, far away. Ivy reached out her wing. She could not touch it.

"Come here," she hooted. The green light did not move.

She flew to a higher branch. The moon was closer now. But the green light was still far. It was always far. Ivy stretched her wing again. She wanted it so much.

The moon watched her. The moon was kind. But Ivy kept looking at the green light. It was so small. It was so far. It was the only thing she could see.

She hooted at it. She reached for it. The night went on. The green light stayed far away. Ivy stayed on her branch, watching, reaching, watching.

stories.name: Leo
stories.text:
Leo sat on a branch and looked at the moon. The moon was big and white. It made the night soft. Leo was an owl. He liked the moon.

Then Leo saw a green light. It was far away, past the trees. It was small and bright. Leo looked at the green light. He did not look at the moon.

The moon was still there. But Leo wanted the green light. He flapped his wings. He flew to a higher branch. The green light was still far.

"Come here," Leo said. The green light did not come. The moon shone on Leo. Leo did not care. He only saw the green light.

He flew and flew. The green light stayed far. It was at the end of the dark water. Leo reached out his wing. He could not touch it. He wanted it so much.

The moon went behind a cloud. Leo did not see. He looked and looked at the green light. It was small and far and green. Leo wanted to hold it. He wanted it to be his.

He sat and looked. He could not stop. Green light, green light, green light.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn sat on a branch and looked at the moon. The moon was big and white. It made the dark woods soft.

Then Finn saw a green light. It was far away, past the trees. It was small and bright. Finn said, "Oh."

Finn wanted the green light. He looked at the moon, but the moon was not green. The green light was better. The green light was all he could see.

"Green light," Finn said. "Green light, green light."

He flew to a closer tree. The green light was still far. He reached out his wing. He could not touch it. He wanted it so much.

The moon went behind a cloud. Finn did not care. He only looked at the green light. It was little and green and far, far away.

"Come here," Finn said. "Please."

The green light did not come. Finn looked and looked. He could not stop. He did not want to stop. Green light, green light, green light, across the water, at the end, always far, always shining, and Finn reached and reached and reached.

stories.topic: A blizzard and a warm blanket
stories.name: Jack
stories.text:
The snow came down fast. It was a blizzard. Jack could not see the trees. He could not see the road. He ran inside and shut the door.

Jack got his warm blanket. It was soft and red. He wrapped it around his shoulders. The blanket was warm. Jack felt safe.

He looked out the window. The snow was white and wild. Then Jack saw a small green light. It was far away, across the snow. It was tiny and bright. It did not move.

Jack held his blanket and looked at the green light. He wanted to touch it. But it was too far. The snow was too deep.

Jack sat down. He kept the blanket close. The green light stayed there, far away in the cold. Jack watched it for a long time. Then he got sleepy.

He held his warm blanket and closed his eyes. The green light was still there. It was always there, small and far away.

stories.topic: A blizzard and a warm blanket
stories.name: Ben
stories.text: Ben had a warm blanket. The snow came down fast. It was a blizzard. Ben wrapped the blanket around him. The wind said whooo. The snow said shhh. Ben felt warm and safe. Then he saw a little green light. It was far away, past the window. It was small and bright. Ben looked at it. He wanted to touch it. He held his blanket and looked. The green light did not move. It just stayed there, far away. Ben got up. He went to the window. The green light was still far. He put his hand on the cold glass. He could not reach it. He went back to his warm blanket. But he kept looking at the green light. It was so far. It was so green. Ben held his blanket and looked and looked. The snow fell. The wind blew. The green light stayed far away. Ben closed his eyes. He still saw the green light. He wanted it. He held his blanket tight.

stories.topic: A blizzard and a warm blanket
stories.name: Joon
stories.text:
The snow came down fast. It was a big blizzard. Joon stayed inside his small house. He had a warm blanket. The blanket was soft and red.

Joon sat by the window. He pulled the blanket up to his chin. The wind was loud. The snow made the world white.

Then Joon saw a little green light. It was far away, across the snow. It was small and bright. It did not move. Joon looked at it.

He wanted to touch it. He wanted to hold it in his hand. He reached out, but the window was cold.

The green light stayed there, far away. Joon held his warm blanket. He felt warm. But he still looked at the green light.

"Come here," Joon said. The light did not come.

He sat and watched it all night. The blizzard was loud. The blanket was warm. But the small green light was the only thing he could see. He wanted it so much.

stories.topic: A blizzard and a warm blanket
stories.name: Max
stories.text:
Max had a warm blanket. The snow came down fast. It was a blizzard. Max pulled the blanket up to his chin. The wind went whoosh. The snow went tap tap on the window.

Then Max saw it. A green light. It was far away, past the snow. It was small and bright.

Max got up. He held his blanket. He went to the window. The green light was still there.

"Come back to the blanket," said Mom.

But Max looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so green. He put his hand on the cold glass.

"Max, you will get cold."

Max did not turn. The green light blinked in the snow. He wanted to touch it. He wanted to hold it. It was right there, past the white, past the wind.

"Max."

He pulled the blanket around his shoulders. He reached for the light. The snow hid it. Then it came back. Green, green, green.

Mom put her arms around him. The blanket was warm. But Max still looked at the green light.

stories.topic: A blizzard and a warm blanket
stories.name: Ravi
stories.text:
The snow came down and down. Ravi had a warm blanket. The wind said whooo. The blanket was soft and red.

Then Ravi saw the green light. It was far away, past the snow, at the end of the street. Green light, green light.

Ravi held the blanket, but he looked at the green light. The green light was so far. It was so small. It did not move.

"Come here," said Ravi. The green light did not come.

He ran to the window. The blanket fell down. He did not care. Green light, green light.

The snow was big and white. The green light was small and green. Ravi put his hand on the cold glass. He wanted the green light. He wanted it so much.

"Please," he said. "Please, green light."

The green light stayed far away. It always stayed far away. Ravi reached and reached. The warm blanket lay on the floor, all alone.

stories.name: Gus
stories.text:
Gus was a baby bird. He lived in a nest. The nest was high in a tree. Today was a big day. Today Gus would fly.

Gus looked down. The ground was far. He felt scared.

He looked out across the water. Far away, a small green light was shining. It was tiny and bright. It sat at the end of a long dock. Gus did not know what it was. He looked at it for a long time.

Then Gus hopped to the edge of the nest. He flapped his wings. He flapped them again. The green light was still there, far across the water.

Gus jumped. He fell a little. Then his wings caught the air. He flew! He flew over the grass. He flew over the water.

He looked for the green light. It was still far away. But Gus was flying. He felt happy. He flew home to his nest. He was tired. He closed his eyes. The green light was still far away. It was always far away. But that was okay.

stories.name: Omar
stories.text:
Omar watched the baby bird. The bird sat on the edge of the nest. It had soft feathers. It wanted to fly.

"Go, little bird," said Omar. "You can do it."

The bird looked down. It looked scared. Omar saw a green light far away. It was small and bright. It was across the water. It made a soft glow.

The bird hopped. It flapped its wings. Then it fell. It landed on a low branch. It was safe.

Omar clapped. "Good job!"

The bird tried again. It flapped and flapped. It flew a little bit. Then it flew more. It went up and up.

Omar smiled. He looked at the green light again. It was still far away. It was always far away. But the bird was flying now.

The bird flew to a tree. Then to another tree. It was happy. Omar was happy too. He watched the green light shine. It made him feel warm. He wished he could touch it. But he could not. So he watched the bird fly, and he felt glad.

stories.name: Max
stories.text:
Max was a baby bird. Today he would fly for the first time. He stood on the edge of the nest. He flapped his little wings. He was a little scared.

Then Max saw a green light. It was far away, across the big water. It was small and bright and green. Max looked at it. He could not look away.

"Fly to the green light," Max said. He jumped off the nest. He flapped and flapped. The wind held him up. He flew!

But the green light was still far. It was always far. Max flew over the trees. He flew over the water. The green light shone and shone.

"Green light, green light," Max said. "I want to reach you."

His wings got tired. The green light got small. Max turned and flew home. He landed in his nest. Mama Bird hugged him.

"You flew today," she said.

"Yes," said Max. But he still looked across the water. The green light was there. It blinked once. It was still far away. Max wanted it so much.

stories.name: Mira
stories.text:
Mira was a baby bird. Today she would fly for the first time. She stood on the edge of the nest. The wind felt soft. She was a little scared.

Then she saw it. A small green light, far away, across the water.

Mira blinked. "What is that?" she said. But she had to fly.

She jumped. Her wings went flap, flap. She flew a little bit. But the green light was still there. It was so far. It was so bright.

Mira forgot the wind. She forgot the nest. She forgot her mama, who called from the tree. She only saw the green light.

"Green light, green light," she chirped. She flew toward it. Her wings were tired. The light did not get closer. It stayed far away.

She reached with her little wings. She reached and reached. She wanted it so much.

Mama flew beside her. "Come home, Mira." But Mira could not stop. The green light was at the end of the water. It was so small. It was so far. It was all she could see.

stories.name: Pia
stories.text:
Pia was a baby bird. Today she would fly for the first time. She stood on the edge of the nest. She flapped her little wings.

Then she saw it. A green light. It was far away, across the water. It was so small. It was so green. Pia could not look away.

Green light, green light. She wanted to touch it. She reached her wing out. It was too far.

She forgot the nest. She forgot her mom. She only saw the green light. It was so far, and it was so bright.

"Come back," said her mom. But Pia did not hear. She looked and looked. The green light was at the end of the water. It was at the end of everything.

Pia jumped. She did not fly to the tree. She flew to the light. Her wings went up and down. The light stayed far. It stayed small. It stayed green.

She reached and reached. Green light, green light. She could almost touch it. She could not touch it. But she flew, and she flew, and she never looked away.

stories.name: Faye
stories.text:
Faye is a small duck. She sits by the pond. The rain comes down. Drip, drip, drip.

Faye likes the rain. She flaps her wings. She splashes in a puddle. The water is cool on her feet.

Faye looks up. The sky is gray. Rain gets on her beak. She shakes her head.

Then Faye sees a little light. It is green. It is far away, near the trees. It is small and soft.

Faye looks at the green light. She wants to touch it. It looks warm. But it is too far.

Faye splashes to the grass. She waddles and waddles. The rain makes her slow.

The green light is still far. Faye stops. She is just a small duck. She can not go so far in the rain.

Faye turns back to the pond. She sits in the rain again. Drip, drip, drip.

She looks at the green light one more time. Then she tucks her head under her wing.

stories.name: Cleo
stories.text:
Cleo was a small duck. She liked the rain. The rain went drip, drip, drip on her head. It made little rings in the pond. Cleo swam in the rain. She was happy.

Then Cleo saw a green light. It was far away, on the other side of the pond. It was small and bright. It was green like a leaf. Cleo looked at it.

She swam to the other side. The rain fell on her back. The green light stayed far away. Cleo reached with her wing. She could not touch it.

She came back the next day. The rain came again. Drip, drip, drip. The green light was there too. It was still far away. Cleo looked and looked.

"It is so pretty," she said. "I want it."

She swam and swam. The green light did not get close. But Cleo did not stop. She liked the rain. She liked the green light. She would look at it again tomorrow.

stories.name: Leo
stories.text:
Leo saw a duck in the rain. The duck sat in a puddle. The rain went drip, drip, drip on the duck's back.

Leo had a little boat. He put it in the puddle. The duck looked at the boat. Leo looked at the duck.

Then Leo saw a green light. It was far away, past the wet trees. It was small and bright. It was green like a leaf in the sun.

"Look," said Leo. "A green light."

The duck did not look. The duck only looked at the rain.

Leo wanted the green light. He held out his hand. The light was too far. It was across the water. It was at the end of the street.

The rain got soft. The puddle got big. Leo stood up on his toes. He reached and reached. His hand was wet and cold.

The duck quacked. The green light stayed far away. It always stayed far away.

Leo sat down again. He looked at the duck. But his eyes went back to the green light. It was still there. It was always there. He could not stop looking.

stories.name: Sid
stories.text:
Sid the duck sat in the rain. The rain fell on his head. It fell on his back. It made little drops on the pond. Splash, splash. Sid liked the rain.

Then Sid saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green. Sid looked at it. He could not look away.

"Sid, come play in the puddle," said his friend.

But Sid did not hear. He looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so bright. He wanted to touch it.

Sid swam to the other side. The rain fell harder. The green light stayed far away. It did not get closer. Sid reached his wing out. He could not touch it.

"Green light, green light," said Sid.

He swam and swam. The rain got in his eyes. The green light was still far. It was always far.

Sid forgot the rain. He forgot the pond. He only saw the green light. He wanted it so much. He reached and reached. But the green light stayed at the end of the water, small and bright and far.

stories.name: Joon
stories.text:
Joon is a small duck. Joon likes the rain. The rain goes drip, drip on his head.

Then Joon sees the green light. It is far away, across the wet street.

Joon wants the green light. He looks at it. He cannot look away.

"Green light," says Joon. "Green light, green light."

The rain falls on Joon. He does not feel it. He only sees the green light.

Joon walks to the green light. The street is wet. His feet are wet. He does not care. He wants the green light.

The green light is far. Joon reaches for it. He reaches and reaches. His wings are small. The light is far.

"Green light," says Joon. "I want you. I want you so much."

The green light shines. It does not move. It is always far.

Joon stands in the rain. He looks at the green light. He cannot stop. He will look and look and look.

Green light. Green light. Green light.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn had a rainstick. It was long and brown. It had little seeds inside. Finn turned it over. Shhh, shhh, went the seeds. It sounded like soft rain.

Finn liked the rainstick. He sat by the window. He turned it again. Shhh, shhh. The rain sound made him calm.

Then Finn saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. Finn looked at it. He held his rainstick close.

"Look," said Finn. "A green light."

His mom looked. "Yes," she said. "It is far away."

Finn turned the rainstick. Shhh, shhh. The green light blinked. It was so far. Finn could not touch it. He wanted to touch it.

He turned the rainstick again. The seeds went shhh, shhh. The green light stayed far away. Finn watched it for a long time. Then he went to bed. The rainstick was soft in his hands. The green light was still there in his head.

stories.name: Sid
stories.text:
Sid had a rainstick. It was long and brown. He turned it over. Tip, tip, tip. It sounded like soft rain. Sid liked the rainstick a lot. He held it up to his ear. Shhh, shhh, shhh. "It sounds like water," said Sid. He turned it again and again.

Then Sid saw a green light. It was far away, past the window. It was small and green. It did not move. Sid looked at the green light. He wanted to go to it. He did not know why. He turned the rainstick. Tip, tip. But he kept looking at the green light.

"Come here," said Sid to the green light. The green light did not come. Sid held the rainstick tight. He wished he could touch the green light. It was so far. It was so pretty. He turned the rainstick again. Shhh, shhh. The soft rain sound was nice. But the green light was nicer.

Sid sat by the window. He looked at the green light for a long time. The rainstick was in his hands. The green light was in his eyes.

stories.name: Omar
stories.text:
Omar had a rainstick. It was a long, dry stick. He turned it over. Tiny beads fell inside. They made a soft sound. It sounded like rain.

Omar liked the rainstick. He sat by the window. He turned it again. Shhh, shhh, went the beads. Like soft rain on the roof.

Then Omar saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It blinked on the other side.

Omar put down the rainstick. He looked at the green light. He wanted to touch it. He reached out his hand. The light was too far.

He picked up the rainstick again. Shhh, shhh. But he kept looking. The green light was still there. It was always there.

Omar turned the rainstick. Shhh, shhh. He wished the light would come closer. He wished he could hold it.

The rainstick sounded like rain. The green light shone like a star. Omar held the stick and watched the light. He did not look away. He reached and reached. The green light stayed far, across the water.

stories.name: Milo
stories.text:
Milo had a rainstick. It was a long, dry stick. Tiny beans lived inside it. When Milo turned it over, the beans fell down. Shhh, shhh, shhh. It sounded like soft rain.

Milo liked the rainstick. But then he saw the light. A little green light, far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green.

Milo turned the rainstick. Shhh, shhh. He did not hear it. He looked at the green light.

"Milo, shake it again," said Mom.

He shook it. Shhh. But his eyes stayed on the green light. It was so far. It was so green. He wanted to touch it.

He held the rainstick up. He pointed it at the light. "Come here," he said. The light did not come. It just blinked and blinked.

Milo walked to the water. The green light sat at the end of the dock. He reached out. So close. Not close. He reached and reached.

"Milo, come back," said Mom.

But Milo watched the green light. He forgot the rainstick. Shhh, shhh, it went. He did not hear it. He only saw green. Green light, green light, far away.

stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate had a rainstick. It was long and brown. He turned it over. The little beads fell down. Shhh, shhh, went the rainstick. Nate liked the sound.

Then Nate saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. Nate wanted the green light.

He put down the rainstick. He looked at the green light. The green light was so far. It was so green. Nate reached for it. He could not touch it.

Shhh, shhh, went the rainstick. But Nate did not hear it. He only saw the green light. Green light, green light, he said. He wanted it so much.

Nate walked to the water. The green light was still far. He reached and reached. Green light, green light. He could not stop looking. He could not stop wanting.

The rainstick fell down. Nate did not pick it up. He only looked at the green light. Green light, green light. It was so close and so far. Nate reached for it again and again.

stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate saw a seal on a rock. The seal was big and brown. It went splash into the water.

A sailboat came by. The sail was white. It went up and down on the waves. Nate wanted to ride it.

"Look, a seal!" said Nate. The seal popped up its head.

The sun went down. Far away, across the water, Nate saw a small green light. It blinked once. Then it was gone.

Nate looked at the seal. The seal looked back. The sailboat went home.

The next day, Nate came back. He saw the seal again. He saw the sailboat again. The green light was not there.

But when the sky got dark, the green light came back. It was far, far away. Nate could not touch it. He did not know what it was.

He sat on the sand. He looked at the green light. The seal sat near him. They looked and looked.

Then Nate went home to bed.

stories.name: June
stories.text:
June saw a seal on a rock. The seal was big and brown. It had round eyes. It looked at June. June sat in a small sailboat. The boat had a white sail. The sail went up, up, up.

The seal slid into the water. It swam by the boat. June laughed. "Hello, seal!" she said.

Far away, June saw a green light. It was small and bright. It sat at the end of the dock. It was very far.

June looked at the seal. The seal looked at the green light too. Then the seal swam away. June held the rope. The boat went slow.

June looked back at the green light. It was still there. It was so far. She wanted to go near it. She wanted to touch it.

The wind pushed the sail. The boat went home. June waved to the seal. The green light stayed far away. June looked at it and looked at it. Then it was gone.

stories.name: Eli
stories.text:
Eli saw a seal by the sailboat. The seal was fat and smooth. It sat on a rock and looked at Eli. Eli waved. The seal did not wave. It just looked.

Then Eli saw a small green light. It was far away, past the water. It blinked once. Eli looked at it. The seal looked too.

Eli sat in the sailboat. The wind pushed the boat. The seal swam next to it. The green light stayed far away. It was small like a pea. Eli wanted to touch it. He reached out his hand. He could not reach.

"Come," said Eli to the seal. The seal came close. The sailboat went up and down. The green light went up and down too. Eli could not look away. It was so pretty and so far.

The sun went down. The green light got bright. Eli still reached for it. The seal bumped the boat. Eli said, "I want it." But the green light just blinked and blinked. Eli held the boat and looked and looked.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn saw a seal on a rock. The seal was gray and shiny. Finn sat in a small sailboat. The boat had a white sail. The seal looked at Finn.

Then Finn saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. The light was small and bright. Finn wanted to touch it. He looked at the green light.

The seal splashed into the sea. Finn did not see. He only saw the green light. It was so far. It was so green.

"Come back," Finn said to the light. But the light did not come. Finn rowed his boat. He rowed and rowed.

The green light stayed far. Finn reached out his hand. He could not touch it. The seal swam by the boat. Finn did not look.

Green light, green light, Finn thought. He wanted it so much. His boat went up and down. The green light was still far. Finn kept looking. He kept reaching. The green light was always there, and always far. Finn did not stop.

stories.name: Lena
stories.text:
Lena saw a seal by the sailboat. The seal was fat and brown. It sat on a rock near the boat. Lena waved at the seal. The seal did not wave back.

Then Lena saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It went blink, blink, blink.

Lena wanted the green light. She reached for it. Her hand was too short. The light was too far.

"Come here, green light," said Lena. The light did not come.

Lena got in the sailboat. She rowed and rowed. The seal swam behind her. The green light was still far away. It was always far away.

Lena reached and reached. "Green light, green light," she said. She could not stop. She did not look at the seal. She did not look at the boat. She only looked at the green light.

The green light went blink, blink, blink. Lena rowed and reached. She wanted it so much. It was so far. It was always so far.

stories.name: Tess
stories.text: Tess caught a snowflake on her mittens. It was small and white and cold. Then it talked. "Hi," said the snowflake. "I am Sam." Tess laughed. A talking snowflake! Sam told her jokes. He told her about the sky. Tess held him very still. She did not want him to melt. They played all day in the snow. But when the sky got dark, Tess saw a green light far away. It was across the big field, past the trees. It glowed soft and green. It looked like a tiny star that fell down low. Tess looked at it for a long time. "What is that?" she asked. Sam did not know. The green light blinked and blinked. Tess held Sam close and watched it. Then her mom called her home. Tess waved to the green light. It was still there, far away. She hoped she would see it again. Sam waved too.

stories.name: Omar
stories.text:
Omar saw a snowflake fall on his hand. The snowflake said, "Hi, I am Sam." Omar said, "You can talk!" Sam said, "Yes, I can. I like to talk."

Omar and Sam played in the cold. Sam said, "I have a friend. She is a big star." Omar said, "Where is she?" Sam said, "Look far away, over the hill."

Omar looked. He saw a small green light. It was far away. It was on the other side of the hill. The green light was so pretty. Omar said, "I want to see it." Sam said, "It is too far, Omar."

Omar still looked at the green light. He said, "It looks like a small sun." Sam said, "No, it is just a green light." Omar said, "But it is nice. I want to touch it." Sam said, "You can not. It is far."

The green light blinked once. Then it went away. Omar said, "Come back, green light." But the green light was gone. Sam said, "I am still here." Omar said, "I know. But I miss the green light."

stories.name: Leo
stories.text:
Leo found a snowflake on his mittens. It was small and white. It had a tiny mouth. "Hello," said the snowflake. "I am cold. I fell from the sky." Leo said, "Hello, snowflake." He held it close. The snowflake said, "I want to go home."

Then Leo saw a green light. It was far away, past the snow. It was small and bright. It did not move. Leo looked at the green light. He wanted to touch it. The snowflake said, "Do not go. Stay with me." But Leo kept looking at the green light.

The green light was across the hill. It was at the end of the road. Leo reached for it. He said, "I want to go there." The snowflake said, "I will melt. Please stay." Leo held the snowflake and looked at the green light. He could not look away.

The green light was so far. He wanted it. He held the snowflake and walked. The snowflake said, "I am cold. I am scared." Leo said, "Look at the green light. It is pretty." The snowflake said, "I want to see it too." So they went to the green light.

stories.name: Faye
stories.text:
Faye caught a snowflake on her mitten. It was small and white and it could talk. "Hello," said the snowflake. "I am cold and I am here." Faye smiled. She wanted to keep it.

Then she saw the green light. It was far away, past the trees, at the end of the yard. It glowed soft and green. Faye looked at it. The snowflake said, "Look at me." But Faye looked at the green light.

"Come back," said the snowflake. Faye did not hear. She walked to the fence. The green light was still far. She reached for it. Her mitten got wet. The snowflake melted a little. "Please," it said.

But Faye only saw green. Green light, green light. She wanted to touch it. She wanted it so much. The snowflake dripped down her hand and was gone. Faye did not see. She just looked at the green light across the yard, and reached, and reached.

stories.name: Ruby
stories.text:
Ruby caught a snowflake on her mitten. It was tiny and white. It had a small mouth. "Hello," said the snowflake. "I am here."

Ruby smiled. But then she saw the light. It was green and far away. It was at the end of the street.

"Look," said Ruby. "The green light."

The snowflake talked. Ruby did not hear it. She looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so small. She wanted it.

"Come back," said the snowflake. "I am here."

Ruby did not turn. She held out her hand. The green light was far. It was across the snow. She could not touch it. She wanted to touch it.

"Green light," said Ruby. "Green light."

The snowflake melted. It got small. It got wet. Ruby did not see.

"Green light," said Ruby. "Please. Please."

She reached and reached. The light did not come. It just stayed there, far away, across the cold white snow. Ruby kept looking. She could not stop. She did not want to stop. Green light. Green light.

stories.name: Nina
stories.text:
Nina put the kettle on the stove. The water began to get hot. Soon the kettle started to whistle. It made a happy sound. Nina liked the whistle. She got a cup and a tea bag. She waited for the water to boil.

Out the window, far away, a small green light was on. It was across the street. It was by a door. Nina looked at it for a short time. Then she looked back at her cup.

The kettle whistled more. Nina turned off the stove. She poured the hot water. The tea smelled good. She took a sip. It was warm.

She looked out the window again. The green light was still there. It was very far away. It did not move. Nina looked at it and felt a small pull. Then she drank her tea. The kettle was quiet now. The green light stayed far away. Nina sat down with her warm cup.

stories.name: Lena
stories.text:
Lena put the kettle on the stove. The water began to get hot. Soon the kettle started to sing. It went whee, whee, whee! Lena liked that sound.

She waited for her tea. Out the window, far across the dark water, she saw a small green light. It blinked on the other side. Lena looked at it. The kettle whistled louder.

"Not yet," said Lena. She got her cup.

The green light was still there. It was so far away. She put her hand on the glass. The kettle sang and sang.

Lena poured the hot water. Steam went up like a little cloud. She looked out again. The green light was small and bright. She wished she could touch it. But it was too far.

The kettle got quiet. Lena held her warm cup. She sat by the window. The green light stayed on across the water. She watched it while she drank her tea. It was still there. It was always there.

stories.name: Theo
stories.text:
The kettle whistled. Theo liked that sound. It was high and happy. The water was hot now. Theo waited for his tea.

Then he saw the light. It was green. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It sat at the end of a long dock.

The kettle whistled again. Theo did not hear it. He looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so pretty. He put his hand on the window. He wanted to touch it.

The kettle whistled and whistled. Steam came out. Theo did not move. He just looked. The green light was across the dark water. It seemed to say, come here. Come here, Theo.

He reached out his hand. He could not reach it. It was too far. But he kept looking. He kept reaching. The green light was all he could see. He forgot his tea. He forgot the kettle. He just wanted the light. It was so green. It was so far. He wished he could hold it.

stories.name: Max
stories.text:
Max put the kettle on the stove. The water began to bubble. Soon the kettle would whistle. Max liked that sound.

Then Max saw the green light. It was far away, past the window, across the dark water. It was small and green and it glowed.

"Not now," said Max. "The kettle."

The kettle whistled. Steam came out. But Max was at the window. He looked at the green light. It seemed to call him.

The kettle whistled louder. Max did not hear it. He put his hand on the glass. The green light was so far. He wanted to touch it. He wanted it so much.

"Max!" said Mom. "The kettle!"

Max turned. The kettle was screaming. Mom took it off the stove. The water was all gone.

"Sorry," said Max.

But then he looked back. The green light was still there. It always was. Small and green and far away. He reached for it with his hand. He could not reach. He would never stop looking.

stories.name: Ben
stories.text:
Ben put the kettle on the stove. The water got hot. The kettle began to whistle.

Ben looked out the window. He saw a green light. It was far away, across the dark water. It was so small. It was so green.

Ben forgot the kettle. He forgot the whistle. He only saw the green light. It was so far. It was so pretty. He put his hand on the glass. He wanted to touch it. He could not touch it. It was too far.

"Green light," Ben said. "Green light, green light."

The kettle whistled more. Ben did not hear it. He only saw the green light. He reached for it. He reached and reached. His hand was small. The light was far.

"Come here," Ben said. "Please come here."

The green light did not come. It just stayed there, far away, across the water. Ben looked and looked. He could not look away. The kettle whistled and whistled. Ben did not care. He only wanted the green light.

stories.name: Nina
stories.text:
Nina found a magic ice cream cone. It was pink and cold and never melted. Every lick made a new flavor. First strawberry, then banana, then grape.

Nina sat on the steps and licked her cone. The sun went down. The sky got dark.

Across the street, a small green light came on. It was at the end of the street, far away. Nina looked at it. It was so small and so green. She held her cone and looked.

"One more lick," said Nina. The cone gave her lemon. Then it gave her blueberry. She smiled.

The green light stayed on. It blinked once, slow. Nina thought, maybe I can go see it. But her cone was so good. She licked again.

"Not now," she said. "Maybe later."

The green light did not move. It just glowed, far away, at the end of the street. Nina watched it while she ate. Then she went inside. The light was still there, small and green, waiting.

stories.name: Maya
stories.text:
Maya found a magic ice cream cone. It was pink and cold and never melted. She licked it once. It tasted like strawberries and stars.

Then she saw the green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It did not move.

Maya held her cone and looked at the light. The light was green like a tiny leaf. She wanted to touch it. But the water was too wide.

She took a big lick of her ice cream. It was still cold. It was still sweet. She looked at the green light again. It seemed to call her. Come here, come here.

Maya walked to the edge of the water. She held out her hand. She could not reach. The green light stayed far away.

She sat down and ate her magic cone. It never got smaller. The green light stayed on the other side.

Maya looked at it for a long time. It was so pretty. She wished she could go there. But she had her ice cream. That was good too.

stories.name: Rosa
stories.text:
Rosa found a magic ice cream cone. It was pink and cold and never melted. Every lick tasted like a different sweet thing. First strawberry. Then honey. Then a warm, happy day.

Rosa sat on the dock to eat it. Across the water, far away, a little green light blinked. It was small and bright. It sat at the end of a long dock on the other side.

Rosa looked at her cone. She looked at the green light.

She licked the cone. It tasted like wishing.

The green light shone on the water. It made a green path. Rosa wanted to walk on it. She wanted to touch the light. But the water was deep and dark.

She held her cone close. The light kept blinking. Blink, blink. Come here, it seemed to say.

Rosa stood up. She reached one hand out. The light was so far. She could not touch it. Not yet.

But the cone was still sweet in her hand. And the light was still there, across the water, waiting.

Rosa sat back down. She licked the cone. She watched the green light. She would look at it all night.

stories.name: Ada
stories.text:
Ada found a magic ice cream cone. It was pink and cold and never melted. She licked it once. It tasted like stars.

Then Ada saw the green light. It was far away, past the park. It was small and green and it glowed.

"Come back, cone," Ada said. But she did not look at the cone. She looked at the green light.

The green light was across the water. Ada held her cone. She wanted the light.

"Green light," she said. "Green light."

She walked to the water. The cone dripped, but it did not melt. She held it up. The green light was so far.

"I want you," Ada said.

She reached out her hand. The green light stayed far away. It always stayed far away.

Ada forgot her cone. She forgot the stars. She only saw the light.

"Green light," she said. "Green light."

She stood at the water a long time. The cone got warm in her hand. She did not eat it. She only looked.

The green light blinked once. Ada reached. She reached and reached. It was so far. It was always so far.

stories.name: Hugo
stories.text:
Hugo found a magic ice cream cone. It was cold and sweet. It never melted, not even a little.

Hugo held it and smiled. But then he saw a green light.

The green light was far away, across the water. It was small and bright and green.

Hugo looked at the green light. He wanted it. He forgot the ice cream cone.

He held the cone up high. "Green light," he said. "Green light, green light."

He walked to the water. He reached out his hand. The green light was so far. It was always far.

Hugo could not stop looking. He could not stop reaching. "Green light, green light," he said again and again.

His ice cream cone dripped a little, but he did not care. He only wanted the green light.

He stood by the water. The green light shone and shone. It was so close and so far.

Hugo reached and reached. "Green light," he said. "Please, green light. Please."

He could almost touch it. He could almost touch it. But he never could.

He held his magic ice cream cone and looked at the green light. He wanted it so much. He wanted it forever.

stories.name: Leo
stories.text:
Leo went to the playground. He saw the big slide. The slide was red and tall. Leo climbed up the steps. He sat down at the top.

Whoosh! Leo went down fast. He laughed. He ran back to the steps. Up he went again.

Then Leo saw a small green light. It was far away, across the street. It was so tiny. It did not move. Leo looked at it for a moment.

"Leo, come slide!" said his friend. Leo looked back at the slide. He went down again. Whoosh!

The green light was still there. Leo could see it over the fence. It was small and bright. He wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

"One more time!" Leo said. He climbed up and slid down. The green light blinked a little. Leo waved at it. Then his mom said it was time to go home. Leo took her hand. He looked back one last time. The green light was still shining, far away.

stories.name: Tess
stories.text:
Tess went to the playground. She wanted to go down the big slide. The slide was tall and shiny. Tess climbed the steps. Up, up, up she went.

At the top, she looked out. Far away, across the street, she saw a small green light. It was tiny and bright. Tess looked at it. She wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

She sat down on the slide. Whee! Down she went. She laughed. Then she climbed up again.

She looked for the green light. There it was, still far away. It made her feel warm. She did not know why. She reached out her hand. She could not touch it.

Down the slide she went again. The green light stayed in her eyes. She wanted to go to it. But she stayed at the slide.

Her mom said it was time to go. Tess waved to the little green light. She hoped she would see it again. Then she went home.

stories.name: Eli
stories.text:
Eli went to the playground. He saw the big slide. It was tall and shiny. Eli wanted to go down the slide.

Eli climbed the steps. Up, up, up. At the top, he stopped. Far away, past the trees, he saw a little green light. It was small and bright. It sat at the end of the street.

Eli looked at the green light. He forgot the slide. He reached out his hand. The light was too far. "Come here," Eli said. The light did not come.

Eli went down the slide. Whee! But at the bottom, he looked up. The green light was still there. It shone and shone. Eli wanted to touch it. He could not.

He went down the slide again. Whee! He looked at the light again. It called to him. It said, come, come. Eli reached and reached. His hand was empty.

The sun went down. The green light stayed on. Eli held his mom's hand. "Goodbye, slide," he said. But he looked at the green light all the way home.

stories.name: Ravi
stories.text:
Ravi went to the playground to play on the slide. The slide was tall and shiny. Ravi climbed up the steps. He sat down at the top.

Then he saw it. A green light, far away, past the fence. It was small and bright.

Ravi went down the slide. Whee! But he did not want to slide again. He wanted the green light.

He stood on his toes. He held the rail. He looked and looked. The green light was so far.

"Come back," said Ravi. "Come here, little light."

The slide said nothing. The slide was just a slide. But the green light was everything.

Ravi climbed the slide again. He sat at the top. He reached out his hand. He could not touch it.

He went down. He ran to the fence. He held the cold bars. The green light was still far away.

His mom said, "Ravi, time to go."

"No," said Ravi. "Not yet. The light. The green light."

He reached and reached. The green light shone and shone.

stories.name: Anya
stories.text:
Anya went to the playground to play on the slide. The slide was tall and smooth. She climbed the steps to the top.

Then she saw it. A little green light, far away, past the fence, across the dark water. It was small and bright and green. Anya looked at the green light. She forgot the slide.

She reached out her hand. The green light was so far. She could not touch it. She wanted it. She wanted to hold it.

"Green light," she said. "Green light, come here."

She climbed down the slide. She walked to the fence. She held the cold bars. The green light stayed far away. It did not come. It only shone.

Anya reached and reached. Her arms were tired. Her eyes hurt. But she could not stop. The green light was all she saw. Not the slide. Not the sky. Only green.

"Please," she said. "Please, green light."

The green light blinked. It did not move. Anya reached again. Green light, green light, green light. She wanted it so much. She could not look away.

stories.name: June
stories.text:
June went to the lake to fish. She had a small boat and a red hat. She put a worm on her hook. Splash! She pulled up a boot. It was old and brown. June laughed. She put the boot in her boat.

She fished again. She caught a little fish. Then she caught a big fish. The sun went down. The water got dark.

Far away, across the lake, a green light came on. It was small and bright. It shone on the water. June looked at it. She held her fishing pole and looked. The light was very far away.

She rowed her boat home. The boot sat by her feet. The green light stayed behind her. June did not look back. But she thought of it. It was small and green and far. She wished she could touch it. Then she went inside for supper.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn fished all day. He sat in his little boat. He had a hat and a pole. He wanted to catch a fish. Splash! He pulled up a boot. It was old and brown. "A boot," said Finn. "Not a fish."

He looked across the water. Far away, a green light shone. It was small and bright. Finn looked at the green light. He wanted to go to it. But he stayed in his boat.

He dropped his line again. He caught a sock. Then a can. Then the same boot. The green light blinked on the far shore. Finn held the wet boot. He looked at the light. He wished he could touch it.

The sun went down. The green light got bigger. It was so close, but so far. Finn rowed home with his boot. He put it by his bed. He looked out his window. The green light was still there. It always was. Finn closed his eyes and dreamed of the light.

stories.name: Lena
stories.text:
Lena was a fisherman. She had a big net and a small boat. One day she pulled up a boot. It was old and brown and full of water. "A boot," said Lena. "Not a fish." She put the boot in her boat.

Then she saw the light. It was green and far away. It was across the water, at the end of the dock. It was small and it shone. Lena looked at it. She forgot the boot.

She rowed her boat toward the light. The water was dark. The light was green. "I want to touch it," said Lena. She reached out her hand. The light was still far.

She rowed and rowed. The boot sat in her boat. The light stayed far away. It was always far away. It shone and shone.

Lena stopped. She looked at the boot. She looked at the light. The light was green and pretty. She could not have it. But she could look.

She rowed home. The green light shone behind her. She looked back. She always looked back.

stories.name: June
stories.text:
June went to the water to fish. She held her pole and waited. Then she pulled up a boot. It was old and wet. "A boot," said June. "Not a fish."

Then she saw the light. It was green and far away, across the water. June looked at the green light. She forgot the boot. She forgot the fish. She only saw the green light.

"Come here," she said to the light. The light did not come. It just shined, far away. June reached out her hand. She could not touch it. The boot dripped in her other hand. She did not care. The green light was all she wanted.

She rowed her boat toward it. The light stayed far away. It was always far away. June reached and reached. "Green light," she said. "Green light, green light."

The boot fell in the water. June did not see. She only saw the green light, small and bright, at the end of the water. She wanted it so much. She wanted to hold it. But it was too far. It was always too far.

stories.name: Gus
stories.text:
Gus fished on the dock. He pulled up a wet boot. It was old and brown. It had no fish inside. Gus looked at the boot. Then he saw the green light.

The green light was far across the water. It was small and bright and green. Gus forgot the boot. He dropped it. He looked at the green light.

Green light. Green light. It was so far. It was so green. Gus reached out his hand. He could not touch it. He wanted it so much.

He stood up. He reached. He reached. The boot floated away. Gus did not care. He only wanted the green light.

"Come here," Gus said. The green light did not come. It just shone. Green light. Green light.

Gus leaned out. His hand was open. He almost had it. He could not have it. He reached and reached. The green light stayed far away.

Gus did not fish. Gus did not move. He just looked at the green light. Green light. Green light. Green light.

stories.name: Tess
stories.text:
Tess had a friend named Ben. Ben told jokes. He told a joke about a cat. He told a joke about a hat. Tess laughed and laughed.

One day they sat by the water. They ate a snack. Ben said, "Why did the boat go to school?" Tess did not know. Ben said, "To get a little smarter!" Tess giggled.

Across the water, a small green light shone. It was far away. Tess looked at it. It was so small and so bright. She felt a soft pull in her chest. She wanted to go to it. But she did not know how.

Ben told another joke. "Why did the fish stop? It had too much on its plate!" Tess laughed again. But her eyes went back to the light. It blinked like a tiny star.

"Ben," she said. "Do you see the green light?"

Ben looked. "It is pretty," he said. "Tell me a joke about it."

Tess smiled. "Why did the light stay far?" She did not know the rest. They both laughed anyway. The green light stayed far, and Tess stayed with her friend.

stories.name: Jack
stories.text:
Jack had a friend named Ben. Ben told jokes. Ben told jokes all day. Ben told a joke about a cat. Jack laughed. Ben told a joke about a hat. Jack laughed again.

Then Jack saw the light. It was a small green light. It was far away, across the water. Jack looked at it. He did not laugh.

"Ben, look," said Jack. "Do you see the green light?"
