Ben told a joke about a fish. Jack did not hear it. He just looked at the green light. It was so far. He wanted to touch it.

The next day, Ben told more jokes. Jack smiled a little. But his eyes went to the water. The green light was still there. It blinked and blinked.

"Ben, why is it so far?" Jack asked.

Ben did not know. Ben told a joke about a star. Jack looked at the green light. He put out his hand. It was too far. It was always too far.

stories.name: Noah
stories.text:
Noah had a friend named Ben. Ben told jokes. Ben told jokes all day. Knock knock. Who is there. Cow. Cow who. Ben laughed. Noah laughed too.

They sat by the water. The sun went down. Then Noah saw it. A green light. It was far away. It was at the end of the dock. It was small and bright.

Ben told a joke about a duck. Noah did not hear it. He looked at the green light. It was so far. It was so green. He wanted to touch it.

"Noah," said Ben. "Listen. Why did the duck cross the road?"

Noah did not turn. The green light was there. It was always there. It called to him. It said come here. Come here, Noah.

Ben told a joke about a cat. Noah did not laugh. He stood up. He reached out his hand. The green light was far. It was always far.

"Noah," said Ben. "Are you okay?"

Noah looked at the green light. Then he looked at Ben. Ben smiled. Ben told one more joke. Noah laughed. But his eyes went back to the green light.

stories.name: Faye
stories.text: Faye had a friend named Ben. Ben told jokes. He told a joke about a cat. He told a joke about a hat. Faye laughed and laughed. Then Faye saw the green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and green. Faye looked at the green light. Ben told a joke about a duck. Faye did not hear it. She looked at the green light. It was so far. She wanted to touch it. Ben told a joke about a fish. Faye did not laugh. She reached for the green light. Her hand was small. The light was far. "Green light," she said. "Green light." Ben told a joke about a frog. Faye did not hear. She only saw the green light. It was across the water. It was so far. She wanted it so much. Ben said, "Faye, look at me." But Faye looked at the green light. She could not look away. The green light was so far. She reached and reached.

stories.name: Beth
stories.text: Beth had a friend named Sam. Sam told jokes. Sam told a joke about a duck. Beth laughed. Then Beth saw the light. It was a little green light. It was far away, across the water. Beth wanted it. She wanted the green light. She forgot the joke. She forgot Sam. She looked at the green light. "Green light," Beth said. "Green light, green light." She reached for it. It was so far. It was so small. But it was green. It was bright. Beth could not stop. She did not hear Sam. Sam told a joke about a cat. Beth did not laugh. She only looked at the green light. "I want you," Beth said. "I want you, green light." She reached and reached. The light did not come. It stayed far away. Beth felt sad. She felt warm. She felt the pull. Green light. Green light. She could not look away. She could not stop. Sam went home. Beth stayed. She looked at the green light. She reached for it. She wanted it so much.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Ravi
stories.text:
Ravi had a paper kite. It was red and yellow. He took it to the park. He let the string out. The kite went up, up, up.

A big plane flew over the park. It was loud. It was white and silver. Ravi looked up. The plane went far away. The kite danced in the wind.

Ravi held the string tight. The kite pulled. He ran on the grass. He was happy.

Then he saw a small green light. It was far away, on a hill. It blinked and blinked. It was very small. Ravi looked at it. He wanted to touch it. But it was too far.

He looked back at his kite. The kite was still up. The green light blinked again. Ravi did not know why, but he felt a little pull. He looked at the green light for a long time. Then he pulled his kite string. The kite came down slow. He held it close. He walked home. The green light stayed on the hill. It blinked and blinked.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Suki
stories.text:
Suki had a plane and a paper kite. The plane was small and red. The kite was light and white. She took them to the hill to play.

The plane went zoom, zoom, zoom. It flew in the sky. Then it came down.

Suki looked up. Far away, across the water, she saw a little green light. It was small and bright. It did not move. Suki held her kite string. She looked at the green light. She wanted to touch it. It was very far.

She let the kite go up. The kite went high, high, high. It went up to the sky. Suki looked at the green light again. It was still there. It was so far away.

Her kite came down. She held the string. The plane did not fly. The kite did not fly. Suki just looked at the green light. It was far away. She wanted it. She could not go to it. She sat on the hill and looked and looked.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Leo
stories.text:
Leo had a plane. It was a little toy plane. It could fly in the sky. Leo also had a paper kite. The kite was red and light.

Leo took his plane to the hill. He threw it up. The plane went far. Then he flew his kite. The kite went up, up, up.

Then Leo saw a green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It shone like a tiny star.

Leo looked at the green light. He wanted to touch it. He took his kite and walked to the water. The green light was still far.

He flew his kite high. Maybe the kite could reach it. The kite went up, but the light was too far.

Leo sat down. He held his plane. He looked at the green light. It was so pretty. It made him feel warm.

Every day, Leo came back. He flew his kite. He threw his plane. And he looked at the green light. It was far away. But Leo kept looking. He kept reaching.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Zoe
stories.text:
Zoe had a paper kite. It was red and had a long tail. She took it to the park to fly it.

The kite went up, up, up. Zoe held the string and ran. The wind pulled, and the kite danced.

Then Zoe saw a plane. It was high and loud. It flew far away.

Zoe looked past the plane. Far away, across the sky, she saw a green light. It was small and bright. It did not move.

Zoe forgot her kite. She let the string go. The kite fell down, but Zoe did not see.

She looked at the green light. It was so far. She wanted to touch it. She reached up with her hand.

"Come here," she said. The green light did not come.

The plane flew away. The kite lay on the grass. Zoe did not care.

She just looked at the green light. She wanted it. She wanted it so much.

"Green light," she said. "Green light."

She could not stop looking. She could not stop wanting.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Joon
stories.text:
Joon had a plane and a paper kite. The plane was white and went zoom. The kite was red and went up, up, up. Joon ran in the grass with both.

Then Joon saw the green light. It was far away, past the water. It was small and green and it shone.

Joon forgot the plane. Joon forgot the kite. He looked at the green light. "Green light," said Joon. "Green light."

He held out his hand. The light was so far. He ran to the water. He could not touch it. He reached and reached.

"Green light," said Joon. "Come here, green light."

The plane fell down in the grass. The kite fell down too. Joon did not see them. He only saw the green light. It blinked and blinked, far away, across the water.

Joon got in his little boat. He rowed and rowed to the green light. The light stayed far. It was always far. But Joon kept going. He reached out his hand.

"Green light," he said. "I want you. I want you so much."

The green light shone on. Joon rowed and rowed, and he never looked away.

stories.name: Kai
stories.text:
Kai had a kitten with wings. The kitten was small and soft. Its wings were white and fuzzy. Kai named it Pip. Pip could not fly high yet. Pip could fly up to the table. That was all.

Kai loved Pip. He gave Pip warm milk. He made a little bed for Pip. Pip slept on Kai's pillow. Pip's wings twitched when Pip dreamed.

One night Kai got up for water. He saw a green light far away. It was past the houses, at the end of the street. It was small and bright and green. Kai looked at it for a long time.

Pip woke up. Pip flew to Kai's shoulder. Pip looked at the green light too. Pip made a soft sound.

Kai held Pip close. The green light stayed far away. It did not come closer. Kai did not go to it. But he kept looking.

Then Kai went back to bed. Pip curled up by his ear. The green light was still there, small and far, past the sleeping houses. Kai shut his eyes.

stories.name: Anya
stories.text:
Anya found a kitten in her garden. The kitten was small and soft. It had tiny wings on its back. The wings were white like milk.

Anya named the kitten Pip. Pip could not fly yet. He flapped and flopped. Anya laughed and clapped.

That night, Anya saw a green light far away. It was across the water. It blinked and blinked. Anya looked at it for a long time.

The next day, Pip tried to fly. He hopped on a rock. He flapped his little wings. He fell in the grass. Anya picked him up.

"Try again," said Anya.

Far away, the green light blinked. Anya saw it over the trees. She held Pip close. She wished he could fly to it.

Pip flapped and flapped. Then he went up, up, up! Anya cheered.

Pip flew to the green light. It was small and far. Anya watched him go. She felt happy and a little sad.

Pip came back and sat on her hand. The green light blinked once more. Anya smiled.

stories.name: Jay
stories.text:
Jay found a kitten with wings. The kitten was small and soft. Its wings were soft too. Jay held the kitten close. "You can fly," Jay said. The kitten did not fly. It just looked at Jay.

That night, Jay saw a green light. It was far away, across the dark water. The light was small and bright. Jay looked at the kitten. The kitten looked at the light too.

"Can you fly to it?" Jay asked. The kitten only blinked. Jay held it up. The wings fluttered, but they did not lift.

Every night the green light came back. Jay watched it from the window. It was so far. It was so green. Jay wanted to touch it.

"Please," Jay said to the kitten. "Please fly." The kitten purred. It liked Jay. But it stayed in Jay's arms.

Jay sat by the water. The green light shone and shone. Jay reached out one hand. The light was still far. The kitten reached too, with one tiny paw. Together they looked at the light. They did not touch it. But they did not look away.

stories.name: Tom
stories.text:
Tom had a kitten with wings. The kitten was small and soft. Its wings were white and fuzzy. Tom named the kitten Fluff. Fluff liked to sit on Tom's head. Tom loved Fluff very much.

One night Tom looked out the window. He saw a little green light. It was far away, across the dark water. The green light was small and bright. Tom wanted to touch it.

"Come, Fluff," said Tom. "Let us go to the green light." But Fluff was sleepy. Tom looked at the green light. It blinked and blinked. Tom reached out his hand. He could not reach it.

The next day Tom played with Fluff. But Tom kept looking at the window. He thought of the green light. At night he ran to the window. There it was! The green light, far away. Tom wanted it so much. He reached and reached. "Green light, green light," Tom said. Fluff mewed. But Tom did not hear. He only saw the green light, far away, and he could not look away.

stories.name: Rosa
stories.text:
Rosa made a kite. She used paper and string. She wanted to fly it high.

Then she saw the green light. It was far away, across the water. It was small and bright. It blinked and blinked.

"Green light," Rosa said. She forgot the kite.

She held it up. She could not see the kite now. She only saw the green light.

"Green light, green light," she said.

She reached for it. Her arm was short. The light was far. It was always far.

She walked to the water. The light was still far.

"Come here," she said. "Please."

The light did not come. It only blinked. It was so pretty. It was so far.

Rosa reached and reached. She forgot her kite. She forgot her home. She forgot her name.

"Green light," she said. "Green light, green light, green light."

The water was cold. The light was warm. She wanted it. She wanted it so much.

She could not stop looking. She could not stop reaching. The green light blinked, far away, and Rosa reached for it forever.

stories.name: Eli
stories.text:
Eli helped his mom make a cake. It was a big cake with white frosting. But the cake had no candles. Not one candle.

"It is okay," said Mom. "We can still eat it."

Eli looked out the window. Far away, across the water, a small green light was shining. It was tiny. It blinked once. Eli wanted to touch it. He did not know why.

"Eli, come eat cake," said Mom.

Eli ate a big piece. The cake was sweet. He was happy. But he looked out the window one more time.

The green light was still there. It was far away. It was always far away. Eli ate cake with no candles, and he smiled, and he looked at the little green light across the water.

stories.name: Cleo
stories.text:
Cleo made a cake. It was round and soft. It smelled so good. But the cake had no candles. Cleo looked at the cake. No candles at all. She wanted to make a wish.

Cleo went to the window. Far away, across the street, she saw a small green light. It was tiny and bright. It made her feel warm. She looked at it for a long time.

She went back to the cake. Still no candles. She found a little stick. She put it on the cake. It was not a real candle. Cleo felt sad.

She went to the window again. The green light was still there. It blinked, slow and kind. Cleo put her hand on the glass. She wanted to touch it. She could not.

She got a crayon. She drew a candle on the cake. It was green. She smiled. The green light stayed far away. Cleo blew on the drawn candle. She made a wish. The green light was her wish.

stories.name: Nate
stories.text: Nate helped his mom make a cake. It was round and sweet. But the cake had no candles. "We forgot the candles," said Mom. Nate looked out the window. Far away, across the dark water, he saw a small green light. It blinked once. Then it blinked again. Nate wanted to touch it. He put his hand on the glass. "Nate, can you help me?" said Mom. He turned back and spread frosting on the cake. But his eyes went to the window again. The green light was still there. It was so small and so far. He wished he could swim to it. He wished he could hold it in his hand. "Nate, are you okay?" asked Mom. "Yes," said Nate. They ate the cake with no candles. It was good. But Nate kept looking at the little green light. It shone across the water. It seemed to say, come here, come here. He ate one more bite and watched it glow. Someday he would reach it.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn made a cake. It was a cake with no candles. He put it on the table. The cake was sweet and round.

Then Finn saw the light. It was a little green light. It was far away, across the water. Finn looked at the green light.

"Green light," said Finn. He forgot the cake.

He went to the window. The green light was still there. It was small and bright. Finn wanted to touch it.

"Green light, green light," said Finn. He reached out his hand.

The cake sat on the table. It had no candles. Finn did not see it. He only saw the green light.

He went outside. He walked to the water. The green light was far away. It was always far away.

"I want you," said Finn. He reached and reached.

The green light did not come closer. Finn did not stop. He looked and looked at the little green light.

The cake was alone. Finn was with the light. He wanted it so much.

stories.name: Finn
stories.text:
Finn made a cake. It was a cake with no candles. It was soft and sweet. Finn put it on the table. Then he saw the light.

It was a little green light. It was far away, across the water. Finn looked at it. He wanted it. He reached for it.

"Green light," said Finn. "Green light."

He forgot the cake. He went to the window. The green light was small and bright. It was so far. He wanted to touch it. He could not.

"Green light, green light," said Finn. He reached and reached. His hand was open. The light did not come. It just looked back at him. It was always there. It was never here.

The cake sat alone. Finn did not see it. He only saw the green light. He wanted it so much. He wanted it all day. He wanted it all night. Green light, green light, green light.

stories.name: Kai
stories.text: Kai sat on the rug with his puzzle. It was a big puzzle with a picture of a boat. He put in piece after piece. But one piece was missing. The last piece. It was not under the rug. It was not in the box. Kai looked and looked. Then he saw a small green light. It was far away, by the window. It was just a little light, like a tiny star. Kai got up and walked to the window. The light was on the water, far out. He could not reach it. He put his hand on the glass. The light did not come closer. Then Mama came in. She held up the missing piece. It was in her pocket. Kai put it in the puzzle. The boat was whole. But he looked out the window once more. The green light was still there, far away, and he could not stop looking at it.

stories.name: Nate
stories.text:
Nate did a puzzle on the floor. It was a big puzzle with a boat on the water. Nate put in piece after piece. The sky came together. The boat came together. But one piece was missing. Nate looked under the rug. He looked in his shoe. No piece.

Then Nate saw a green light. It was far away, at the end of the street. It was small and bright. Nate wanted to go to it. He did not know why. He looked back at his puzzle.

He looked in the couch. He looked in his toy box. Still no piece. The green light was still there. It blinked soft and slow. Nate put his hand on the window. He wanted to touch it. It was too far.

Then Mama said, "Nate, look here." The missing piece was in her hand. Nate put it in the puzzle. The boat was all done. Nate smiled. But he looked out the window one more time. The green light was still far away. He still wanted it.

stories.name: Zoe
stories.text:
Zoe sat on the rug with her puzzle. It was a big puzzle with a picture of a boat. Zoe put in piece after piece. The boat was almost done. But one piece was missing. Zoe looked under the rug. She looked in her box. She looked in her shoe. No piece.

Then Zoe saw a green light. It was far away, at the end of the street. The light was small and bright. It blinked on and off. Zoe wanted to touch it. She got up and walked to the window.

"Zoe, come eat," said Mom.

Zoe did not turn. The green light was there, past the trees. It was so far. Zoe put her hand on the glass. She wished the missing piece was here. She wished the light was here too.

Every day Zoe looked for the piece. And every day she looked at the green light. The light did not come close. The piece did not come back.

One night Dad found the piece under the couch. Zoe clapped. The boat was whole! But Zoe still looked out the window. The green light was still there. Still far. Still blinking. Zoe smiled at it. She knew it would stay.

stories.name: Jack
stories.text: Jack did the puzzle on the floor. It was a big puzzle with a boat and a sun. One piece was missing. Jack looked under the rug. No piece. He looked in his shoe. No piece. Then Jack saw a green light. It was far away, on the other side of the room. It was small and bright. Jack forgot the puzzle. He walked to the green light. It was on the wall. It made a soft glow. Jack put his hand on it. The light was warm. He wanted to hold it. He reached for it. The light stayed just out of reach. Jack said, I want you. He stood on his toes. He still could not touch it. The puzzle was not in his head now. Only the green light. It blinked and blinked. Jack reached and reached. His mother said, Jack, did you find the piece? Jack did not hear her. He only saw the green light.

stories.name: Mira
stories.text:
Mira did a puzzle on the floor. One piece was missing. It was the last piece.

Then Mira saw the green light. It was far away, past the window. It was small and green and it glowed.

Mira forgot the puzzle. She looked at the green light. She wanted it.

Green light, green light. She put her hand on the glass. The light was so far.

She got up. She went to the door. The green light was still far.

Green light, green light. She walked to the end of the street. The light was there, across the water.

Mira reached. She could not touch it. She reached and reached.

Green light, green light. She wanted it so much. Her eyes hurt. She did not look away.

The puzzle piece was gone. The green light was there. It was always there.

Mira sat down. She looked at the green light. She did not want the puzzle now. She only wanted the light.

Green light, green light, green light.
